text:
toby: heads-up — hit a weird parity bug in the next-langchain-agent-lite starter. UI shows smooth streaming answer but Console shows doubled token counts for streamed responses.

kevin: doubled tokens? repro steps?

toby: repo: github.com/redwood/samples/next-langchain-agent-lite. Steps: yarn; vercel dev; open /chat; ask a question; watch Console token_meter spike to ~2x the expected. Screenshot attached locally.

anna: does the browser stream + server handler both call the model? maybe both sides are instrumented and each emits telemetry.

toby: it's a single endpoint; browser opens a websocket-ish stream via EventSource to the server, server streams tokens using Redwood.streams. But the SDK's streaming helper in the starter does a fallback that replays the token chunk to a `onpartial` hook which then calls telemetry.track('tokens', {count}) — i.e. tokens get tracked twice: once by the runtime (auto telemetry) and once by starter code.

kevin: ah, double-instrumentation. Two fixes: stop manual token-track in starter and rely on SDK telemetry, or disable SDK auto token telemetry and keep starter instrumentation. Prefer relying on SDK to avoid missing cases.

toby: created quick patch removing manual token tracking in the stream handler. But discovered another issue: when people copy starter to use LangChain agents, a common pattern is to call the model once for planning + again for execution — sample didn't show cost caveat. That pattern easily doubles billing and novices copy it.

anna: we should add a comment in the agent sample explaining "planner vs executor" calls count separately and show how to use `Redwood.callPlan({ planOnly: true })` (if you want cost-free planning) — or better, use a single-call agent pattern.

sdk-bot: note: SDK has an opt-out flag `telemetry: {autoTokenMetrics: false}` in v0.13+, so templates can explicitly opt-out if they instrument manually. Recommend templates depend on v0.13.1+.

kevin: action items: 1) update next-langchain-agent-lite to remove manual token telemetry and rely on SDK auto metrics, 2) add a clear README section "Streaming & agent cost patterns" with example showing single-call agent wiring, 3) pin @redwood/inference-js >=0.13.1 in template, 4) add a tiny CI smoke test that runs the sample locally and asserts token meter increments once per request.

qa: failing test in pipeline: integration/streams-agent.test.js -> observed token delta 2x expected. We'll accept the patch that removes manual instrumentation and adds README.

toby: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/samples/pull/3999 "langchain-agent-lite: fix double-stream telemetry, pin SDK, docs" — removes manual telemetry and adds dev note about planner/executor costs.

anna: small UX suggestion: add a dev-only debug banner in the starter that shows `tokens_sent_last_request` and flags if it's > 1x expected. Helps novices spot accidental double calls.

kevin: +1. Also consider adding an example using LangChain tools that runs the planner locally (no call) and only calls model for final execution to show tradeoffs.

toby: created issue #1912 (devex) "next-langchain-agent-lite: streaming double-count & agent cost docs" and linked PR 3999.

kevin: thanks for catching this — very easy to copy incorrectly. Good call removing redundant telemetry calls.

qa: CI green on updated test after PR. Closing local failure.

toby: merging now. will follow up to add the debug banner in a separate patch. :shipit:
